topic: Why an AI judge picks the wrong ad

slides.title: Your AI ad judge is *biased*
slides.sub: 4 quiet biases that rig your copy tests, and the fix for each.

slides.title: Testing the model, not the audience
slides.body: Ask a model which ad is better and the answer often reflects its **habits**, not your customer's behaviour. Research on LLM judges documents the pattern.
slides.source: Source: Zheng et al. 2023, "Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena"

slides.title: It favours whoever goes first
slides.body: Swap the order of the same two ads and the verdict can flip. That is position bias.
slides.fix: Judge every pair twice with the order swapped. Keep only the verdicts that survive.

slides.title: It loves the longer version
slides.body: Longer copy reads as more thorough, so the judge rewards length instead of clarity.
slides.fix: Match word counts before judging, and score clarity and specificity separately.

slides.title: It likes its own writing
slides.body: A judge tends to rate text in its own style higher. If one model writes and judges, it grades itself.
slides.fix: Use a different model as the judge than the one that wrote the ads.

slides.title: One overall score hides the reason
slides.body: A single 1 to 10 score drifts between runs and cannot tell you why an ad won.
slides.fix: Replace it with 4 yes/no checks: specific hook, one claim, a real number, one call to action.

slides.title: Trust the judge last
items: Swap the order, run it twice
Check it against real past results
slides.body: Take ads where you already know the click rate. If the judge cannot rank those, do not let it rank new ones.

slides.title: The whole thing
slides.source: A model that cannot rank your past winners cannot rank your next ad.

slides.title: Save this for your next copy test
slides.sub: More rare, high-signal AI x marketing, no generic tips.

caption: Your AI ad judge has a favourite.
It's not your best ad.
Models that rank copy lean on habits:
→ the option shown first
→ the longer option
→ their own writing
→ one vague overall score
The fix stack:
→ Yes/no rubric, not one score
→ Swap the order, run it twice
→ A different model as judge
→ Check it against ads with known results
I'd rather spend an hour testing the judge than a month running ads it picked.
Source: Zheng et al. 2023, LLM-as-a-Judge (MT-Bench).
